extracted.subtask_description: Short, practical rules and craft principles for writing fiction (both functional/habit advice and higher-level aesthetic criteria) aimed at keeping a writer productive and improving story quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take a pencil to write with on aeroplanes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pens leak. But if the pencil breaks, you can't sharpen it on the plane, because you can't take knives with you. Therefore: take two pencils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical preparation: bring two pencils when flying to avoid losing the ability to write due to leaks or breakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: If both pencils break, use a nail file to sharpen
rubrics_metrics.description: If both pencils break, you can do a rough sharpening job with a nail file of the metal or glass type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry a metal or glass nail file as a lightweight contingency tool for sharpening pencils when blades aren't allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take something to write on
rubrics_metrics.description: Take something to write on. Paper is good. In a pinch, pieces of wood or your arm will do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always have a physical or digital surface available to capture ideas immediately; improvisation is acceptable if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard new text with a memory stick
rubrics_metrics.description: If you're using a computer, always safeguard new text with a memory stick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make routine backups of in-progress work (external drives / flash drives) to prevent data loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do back exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Do back exercises. Pain is distracting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to physical wellbeing (posture, back health) because discomfort interferes with focus and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold the reader's attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold the reader's attention. (This is likely to work better if you can hold your own.) But you don't know who the reader is, so it's like shooting fish with a slingshot in the dark. What fascinates A will bore the pants off B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make engagement a central craft goal; write with energy and clarity to sustain attention, while recognizing reader tastes vary and can't be fully predicted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a thesaurus, rudimentary grammar book, and a grip on reality
rubrics_metrics.description: You most likely need a thesaurus, a rudimentary grammar book, and a grip on reality. This latter means: there's no free lunch. Writing is work. It's also gambling. You don't get a pension plan. Other people can help you a bit, but essentially you're on your own. Nobody is making you do this: you chose it, so don't whine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain practical tools and realistic expectations: use reference books, accept that writing requires labor, risk, self-reliance, and professional resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: You can never read your own book with innocent anticipation
rubrics_metrics.description: You can never read your own book with the innocent anticipation that comes with that first delicious page of a new book, because you wrote the thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize limitations in self-reading; understand that revising and judging your own work requires strategies to approximate fresh-reader perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't sit down in the middle of the woods (when blocked)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't sit down in the middle of the woods. If you're lost in the plot or blocked, retrace your steps to where you went wrong. Then take the other road. And/or change the person. Change the tense. Change the opening page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stuck, backtrack to the last known working point and try alternative choices (change POV, tense, opening, plot direction) rather than staying stalled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use varied strategies to overcome blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Prayer might work. Or reading something else. Or a constant visualization of the holy grail that is the finished, published version of your resplendent book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ diverse tactics — spiritual, stimulative (read other work), and visualization of publication — to motivate and unblock creative progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold the reader's attention (central quality stance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold the reader's attention (#6 — the central rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atwood frames reader engagement as the central measure of quality; prioritize storytelling choices that sustain interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write the truth, not just the comfortable truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the truth, not just the comfortable truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for honesty and depth in subject matter and portrayal rather than easy, reassuring versions of reality; confrontation of difficulty is a mark of strong work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice is everything
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a distinctive voice as a primary element of literary quality; voice shapes how material is perceived and felt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre is a tool, not a hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre is a tool, not a hierarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use genre conventions pragmatically to serve story goals rather than ranking genres by perceived value; adapt and borrow as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: The writer is not the speaker; respect the distance
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer is not the speaker; respect the distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain critical separation between author and narrative voice/characters; avoid conflating personal opinions with a narrator's statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form discoveries are essential — don't write the same book twice
rubrics_metrics.description: Form discoveries are essential — don't write the same book twice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek formal experimentation and new structural approaches to keep work fresh and avoid repetition across projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor difficulty; don't simplify for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor difficulty; don't simplify for safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confront hard subjects and complex truths rather than diluting them to avoid discomfort; literary integrity often requires difficulty.
